data.description: Advanced passive structures and causative forms
learningPoints: Develops mastery of advanced passive constructions.
Strengthens formal reporting structures used in academic texts.
Builds control of causative and impersonal constructions.
Improves structural sophistication in professional communication.
Enhances clarity and objectivity in formal writing.

sections.explain: Formal reporting uses 'It is believed that…' structure.

words.word: It is believed that the policy will improve public health.
It believes that the policy will improve public health.
It is believing that the policy will improve public health.

sections.explain: Structure: Subject + is said to + base verb.

words.word: The company is said to be expanding internationally.
The company is said that it is expanding internationally.
The company said to be expanding internationally.
She had her car repaired last week.
She had repaired her car last week (no causative meaning).
She had her car repair last week.

sections.explain: 'Get' passive often implies unexpected or negative events.

words.word: He got promoted after the evaluation.
He got promote after the evaluation.
He was get promoted after the evaluation.
The proposal must be approved before implementation.
The proposal must approved before implementation.
The proposal must be approve before implementation.

sections.explain: Structure: modal + have been + past participle.

words.word: The issue may have been resolved already.
The issue may have resolved already.
The issue may been resolved already.

sections.explain: 'It is expected that…' is common in academic writing.

words.word: It is expected that the results will vary.
It expects that the results will vary.
It is expecting that the results will vary.

sections.explain: Past participle clauses can replace full passive clauses.

words.word: The data collected during the study were carefully analysed.
The data collect during the study were carefully analysed.
The data were collected during the study carefully analysed.

sections.explain: Structure: will have + object + past participle.

words.word: She will have her presentation reviewed before submission.
She will have reviewed her presentation before submission (no causative).
She will have her presentation review before submission.

sections.explain: Structure: was reported to have + past participle.

words.word: The minister was reported to have resigned.
The minister was reported that he resigned.
The minister was report to have resigned.
